limitations: Native requirement mapping is preserved; independent semantic coverage and targeted positive/negative/equivalent game fixtures have not been qualified.

requirements.obligation: Application opened.
Enter the default game entry.
Show the CHOMP title, saved High Score, and working Start, Options and Quit choices on a dark screen.
Do not begin a run behind the main menu.
Large white title, readable choices and hover/focus feedback.
With no save, High Score is 0; returning to this menu never silently starts a run.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Main menu, death overlay, pause menu or a terminal result screen.
Activate Start or Restart.
Begin the maze in Figure 6A with score 0, three lives, all 299 ordinary dots, four energizers, no fruit and no capture chain.
The player starts at P facing and travelling right; red starts at R, cyan/pink/orange at their listed home cells.
The first mode is Scatter.
No inherited pickups, active timers, input buffer or ghosts from the preceding run.
The play view and HUD replace the menu; movement begins.
A fresh run has a new run identity.
Publish its initial state before motion, as defined in Section 6.4.
A fresh maze is displayed.
Observe and traverse its corridors.
Reproduce Figure 6A as a 30-column by 28-row maze, including all wall cells, blocked void cells, ordinary-dot cells, four energizers, the home gate and three paired wrap passages.
Cells are square; scale is free.
Do not shrink the board, remove branches, open wall shortcuts or replace the playfield with a small demonstration maze.
A dense, continuous maze with recognizable central ghost home and perimeter corridors.
The full diagram is part of this requirement; rotating the entire world is allowed if controls and reported coordinates retain the diagram semantics.
Playing with a valid corridor ahead.
Press W/A/S/D or an arrow key.
W/Up requests up, S/Down down, A/Left left and D/Right right in the board diagram.
Move smoothly along corridor centers at 6 cells per active second, within 5%.
Releasing the key continues the current direction until blocked.
No diagonal movement, tile skipping, key-repeat speed changes or movement driven by observer commands.
The character visibly travels and turns to face travel.
At a wall, stop at the last legal cell center; no movement is also a valid blocked result.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Approaching an intersection.
Request a perpendicular turn before reaching it.
Take the requested turn at the first reachable corridor center while the key is held or within 0.25 seconds after release.
If it is illegal there, continue the current legal direction.
No corner cutting or snapping through a wall.
A smooth center-aligned turn.
A released request expires after 0.25 active seconds; the most recently pressed direction wins.
Opposite held keys use the latest press.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Travelling between centers.
Request the opposite direction.
Reverse promptly within 0.10 active seconds if the corridor behind is legal, without waiting for the next center.
No position jump, duplicate pickup or loss of alignment.
Facing and travel reverse.
Repeated reversals remain stable; a blocked request cannot cross a wall.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Player or a roaming/returning ghost reaches a T boundary.
Continue outward through that passage.
Reappear at its opposite listed T cell, preserve direction, and continue normal travel.
The top and bottom T cells pair; each side T pairs with the same row on the opposite side.
No travel through other borders, across the middle of the maze, or through the home gate as the player.
The moving character exits one edge and appears at the paired edge.
Distance travelled across the seam is one cell; no long camera sweep across the board or repeated scoring on wrap.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Playing with an ordinary dot at the player cell.
Cross the dot.
Remove that dot once, add 10 score, increase consumed ordinary dots by one and decrease remaining ordinary dots by one.
No points for empty cells, repeated overlap or another actor consuming the dot.
The dot disappears and the score updates.
Dots at T and F follow the same rule.
P, R, home and gate start without dots.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Playing with an energizer present.
Touch the energizer.
Remove it once, add 50 score and enter Frightened for 5.0 active seconds.
Roaming non-returning ghosts become vulnerable and change appearance.
Energizers do not change the ordinary-dot count or alone satisfy maze completion.
The large orb disappears; frightened ghosts and the empowered player visibly change.
A returning ghost stays harmless and returning; waiting ghosts become vulnerable when they emerge during the active period.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Frightened is already active.
Collect another energizer.
Add another 50 and refresh the remaining frightened duration to 5.0 seconds.
Preserve the current capture-chain count until the continuous frightened period ends.
Do not stack duration, leave an earlier expiry active, or reset the capture multiplier on refresh.
Empowered appearance continues without flickering back to normal.
At expiry restore normal appearance and behavior, clear the capture chain, and resume the suspended wave remainder.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A run is playing.
Observe the pursuers.
Maintain exactly four distinct ghosts: red, cyan, pink and orange.
Normal and frightened speed is 2 cells per active second; returning speed is 4, each within 5%.
They navigate legal corridors and wrap passages.
No wall penetration, teleporting pursuit, extra pursuers or a single shared pursuit personality.
Each ghost remains distinguishable by its normal color and rounded silhouette.
Home/gate traversal is reserved for ghosts entering or leaving home.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Fresh run or life recovery.
Accumulate ordinary dots.
Red begins outside.
Cyan must begin leaving at 30 consumed ordinary dots, pink at 60 and orange at 90, within 0.15 active seconds of reaching the threshold.
At life recovery, waiting ghosts whose thresholds are already met must begin leaving within the same bound, in cyan, pink, orange order.
No premature threshold release caused by energizers, fruit or ghost points.
Waiting ghosts are visible inside home and exit through the gate.
Returning ghosts rejoin independently of the initial threshold.
Already released ghosts are not returned home at a threshold.
Section 6.4 defines departure start, inactivity selection and recovery eligibility.
At least one initial-release ghost is still waiting.
Spend 5.0 active seconds without eating an ordinary dot.
Force the next waiting ghost out in cyan, pink, orange order.
Restart the inactivity clock after a forced release or ordinary-dot pickup.
Do not force all waiting ghosts out at once or use wall-clock time while paused.
One additional pursuer leaves home even if the player is stationary.
Repeat after another 5.0 seconds if a ghost still waits; fresh run and recovery restart this clock.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Normal ghost behavior is active.
Allow active play time to pass.
Use Scatter 5s, Chase 5s, Scatter 5s, Chase 5s, Scatter 5s, Chase 5s, Scatter 5s, then Chase for the rest of that life.
During Scatter each ghost patrols between its two corner-region cells in Table 6B.
No wave advancement during pause, death recovery or frightened time.
Ghost motion alternates between corner patrol and pursuit.
After fright expiry continue the remaining time of the interrupted wave; recovery after a lost life starts a fresh wave sequence.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Red is roaming in Chase.
The player moves to a different corridor.
Red pursues the player's current cell, refreshing its pursuit as it reaches corridor centers.
No fixed waypoint loop presented as chasing.
Red visibly follows the player through legal routes.
Any shortest legal route, including wraps, is acceptable; equally short routes can differ.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Pink is roaming in Chase.
The player changes heading.
Pink pursues the reachable cell up to four cells ahead in the player's current direction, stopping the look-ahead at the first wall, gate or board edge.
Do not always target the current player cell when a distinct ahead cell exists.
Pink attempts to intercept ahead.
A stationary player retains the last facing; if no ahead cell is legal, the player cell is the target.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Cyan is roaming in Chase.
The player or red ghost changes position.
Cyan's pursuit destination is the reflection of red's current cell across the point up to two legal cells ahead of the player.
If that reflected destination is blocked or outside, the target is a roaming cell with minimum straight-line distance to it.
Equally near targets may use any reproducible choice.
No permanently identical red/pink/cyan targets when their defined destinations differ.
Cyan visibly chooses an approach affected by both player heading and red position.
Section 6.4 defines look-ahead limits, nearest-cell sampling and target-refresh boundaries; no search algorithm or data structure is prescribed.
Orange is roaming in Chase.
The player crosses orange's distance boundary.
At straight-line distance less than 8 cells orange pursues the current player cell; at distance 8 or greater orange patrols its corner region.
Do not retreat when closer than 8 cells or pursue the player at distance 8 cells or greater.
Orange alternates between nearby pursuit and distant retreat.
Distance uses displayed board coordinates without wrap-distance shortening; reconsider at corridor centers.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A vulnerable roaming ghost is frightened.
It reaches a corridor decision.
At a corridor center, choose a legal next center that increases shortest legal corridor distance to the player's cell when one exists.
Count paired wraps as one step.
If no next center increases distance, choose one with the greatest available distance.
Keep the 2-cell/second speed.
No wall crossing, indefinite paralysis or hidden invulnerability.
The ghost retreats with its frightened appearance.
Section 6.4 defines the distance, target cell, reversal and tie boundaries.
Equal allowed choices may differ but must be reproducible under the same seed and action timing.
Player contacts a frightened ghost.
Their collision areas overlap.
Capture that ghost once without losing a life; successive captures in one continuous frightened period award 200, 400, 800, 1600, then double again for each further capture.
Repeated overlap with the same returning ghost cannot award points.
The colored body disappears or becomes a clearly reduced returning form; score changes.
The chain resets at frightened expiry, death or fresh run, and is preserved on energizer refresh.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A ghost has been captured.
Allow it to return home.
Travel visibly through corridors and the gate to its home cell at returning speed, remain harmless en route, and then resume roaming.
It is frightened again if the global frightened period is still active.
No instant disappearance/reappearance, permanent removal, harm or recapture while returning.
A distinct returning form moves back to home and its normal/frightened body reappears.
A new run or life recovery cancels the old return journey.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Playing and touching a dangerous ghost.
Collision occurs.
Lose exactly one life, enter a death interval, stop active play and show the death feedback.
Multiple same-time dangerous contacts cause only one life loss.
Show an enabled, clickable Restart control during dying within 0.15 seconds.
No further score, movement, pickup, ghost release or damage during the death interval.
The player disappears or visibly dies, accompanied by a brief camera impulse and updated lives.
Frightened and returning ghosts are not dangerous.
FLOW-04 and Section 6.4 define simultaneous contacts, death timing and the normal Restart route.
A nonfinal life was lost.
The 3.0-second death interval ends.
Respawn the player at P facing right and reset ghost positions to their starting cells.
Preserve current score, collected dots/energizers and fruit-spawn thresholds already spent.
Remove any active fruit; clear fright, capture chain, turn buffer and old motion.
No board refill, score reset, duplicate actors or delayed changes from the lost life.
Normal play resumes on the partially cleared maze with one fewer life.
Restart wave and inactivity clocks and resume rightward player motion.
A new run resets the whole board
Section 6.4 defines the recovery boundary.
A collision reduces lives to 0.
The final lethal contact starts the death interval.
At the end of the 3.0-second death interval after that lethal contact, show GAME OVER with final score, saved high score and Restart, Main Menu and Quit.
TIME-01 tolerance applies to this single deadline.
Keep the terminal world frozen.
No automatic respawn, negative lives, further score or resumed AI.
Clearly distinct losing result screen.
The 3-second limit includes the death feedback; no second interval follows it.
Movement and pause do not dismiss the result.
Restart during dying follows Section 6.4.
Playing after a fresh run, recovery or previous extra-life grant.
Earn score.
Track points earned since that reset.
When at least 2000 have accumulated and lives are below 3, award one life and reset this progress to 0.
Never exceed 3 lives.
No repeated grant from an unchanged score or negative progress on Restart.
An additional yellow life icon appears with a perceptible positive pulse.
At 3 lives do not grant; accumulated progress can remain until a later eligible positive score change, but life recovery resets it to 0.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
An ordinary-dot pickup reaches consumed count 70 or 170.
The threshold is reached exactly once.
Spawn a visible pineapple at F for 10.0 active seconds.
At 170 spawn only if the earlier pineapple is absent; if one is still active, skip that second opportunity without queuing it.
No spawn from score thresholds, duplicate pineapple, delayed second spawn or repeat after death.
A small orange/gold fruit with a green crown appears in the maze.
Pause freezes its lifetime.
Expiry removes it without awarding points; a new run restores both opportunities.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A pineapple is present.
The player contacts it before expiry.
Remove it once and award 1000 score.
No repeated overlap reward or ordinary-dot count change.
Score increases, a brief pineapple-themed reward overlay appears and a short camera impulse is visible.
Fruit disappears on death or terminal transition without points.
At exactly its expiry time, expiry wins.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
At least one ordinary dot remains.
Play, consume energizers, fruit or ghosts.
Continue the run until all ordinary dots are gone.
No early victory from score, time, energizers or fruit.
The board remains playable and the score/lives HUD remains active.
The victory condition counts ordinary dots only.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
The player collects the final ordinary dot.
Resolve the pickup.
Award its 10 points and show YOU WIN within 0.5 seconds with final score, high score, pineapple stage emblem and Restart, Main Menu and Quit.
Freeze movement, damage, scoring, AI and spawning.
Do not require leftover energizers or fruit, or permit late death to replace the win.
A winning result screen distinct from GAME OVER.
If the final dot and a dangerous ghost are touched in the same simulation step, the final-dot win takes priority.
There is one complete maze, not an extra hidden level.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Active play.
Press P or Escape once.
Open a pause overlay with Resume, Restart, Options, Main Menu and Quit.
Freeze positions, score, lives, wave time, fright time, fruit lifetime and release inactivity time.
No gameplay key leakage or wall-clock expiry behind the overlay.
A dimmed/blurred view remains behind readable pause choices.
Resume or a second P/Escape returns to the same state; held keys cannot trigger repeated toggles.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Pause menu, death overlay or terminal result.
Activate Restart.
Start the complete fresh state in FLOW-02 even while frightened play, return travel, fruit expiry or a death interval was in progress.
No old effect, held/queued direction, damage, award or pickup alters the new run.
The clean maze and three lives reappear.
Repeated Restart works; high score and applied settings survive.
Section 6.4 defines death-overlay access and simultaneous-event priority.
Pause, Options or a terminal result.
Navigate Back or Main Menu as appropriate.
Back from Options returns to its originating menu
Main Menu ends the current run and returns to the title screen.
No orphan overlay, invisible modal control, active play behind the menu or lost input focus.
The requested menu and its usable controls appear.
Repeated Options navigation does not duplicate controls or resume a paused run.
Main Menu discards the run while preserving high score and applied settings.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A menu containing Quit.
Activate Quit.
Save the high score and applied options, then close normally.
No background game process left running.
The game window closes.
Standard OS close performs the same persistent-data save.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Options opened from title or pause.
Change the displayed choices.
Expose Window Mode (Windowed, Fullscreen), VSync (Enabled, Disabled), Graphics (Low, Medium, High, Epic, Cinematic) and Resolution.
Offer 1280x720 and 1920x1080 when the desktop supports them; keep unsupported resolutions unavailable.
Do not show choices that cannot be changed or silently apply a pending selection.
Left/right selectors and the selected values are legible
Apply/Revert indicate whether changes are pending.
Use an explicit custom label when existing engine settings do not match a preset.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Options have pending changes.
Activate Revert or Back without Apply.
Discard pending choices and retain the last applied settings.
No unintended resolution, quality or VSync changes.
Revert restores the displayed applied values
Back returns to the originating menu.
With no changes, Apply and Revert are disabled or harmless.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Options have valid pending changes.
Activate Apply.
Apply the actual window mode, resolution, VSync and graphics preset, save them, and continue showing usable UI at the new dimensions.
No decorative-only settings or stretched/unreachable menu after resize.
The window/rendering change and selected labels agree.
Reopening the application preserves applied settings; a launch-time viewport override may temporarily override window size for a session.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A score exceeds the existing best.
Continue play, return to menu, quit and reopen normally.
High score is the maximum achieved score, visible on the title and result screens and preserved across process restart.
No decrease after a weaker run, Restart or returning to menu.
The new record is identified on the result screen.
On first launch or unreadable save, start safely at 0 without corrupting the playable flow.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A partially played run was closed.
Open the application again.
Open the main menu with the saved best and applied settings.
Starting then begins a fresh run.
Do not restore partial score, lives, remaining pickups, fruit, frightened state or terminal state as a resumed run.
Title screen appears before a new clean play session.
A fresh process identity distinguishes reopening from in-process Restart.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Playing or paused.
Score or lives change.
Show SCORE at the upper left and LIVES with yellow open-mouth icons at the lower left.
Update both within 0.15 seconds of a change; the icon count equals current lives.
No stale number, negative count, cropped text or overlap obscuring the player near the screen center.
Large thin white labels and clearly separated yellow icons.
At 1280x720 and 1920x1080 the information stays readable; terminal screens may replace the HUD.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Viewing active play.
Inspect the maze and move through it.
Render a real 3D perspective maze: near-black cuboid walls with thin electric-blue emissive edges, dark walkable floor, visible wall height and shaded side faces.
White luminous dots sit along corridor centers; energizers are visibly larger.
Retain bloom without washing out corridor boundaries.
No flat diagram, unlit debug boxes, missing materials or HUD drawing used as the entire world.
Dark neon arcade composition with visible depth and a dense full-sized maze.
Geometry and rendering technique are free within ASSET-04; keep wall height between 0.65 and 1.10 cell and dot diameter between 0.12 and 0.25 cell.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Player moving and turning.
Travel along corridors.
Show a luminous yellow spherical character with a visibly opening/closing mouth, dark eyes and pale triangular teeth.
Animate repeated chomping while moving, oriented along travel.
No static sphere, permanently closed mouth, backward-facing travel or animation detached from the character.
Readable biting silhouette and animated mouth at normal camera distance.
Body diameter is 0.55 to 0.85 cell; open mouth animation also remains readable in frightened play.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Four ghosts are visible.
Normal, frightened and returning states occur.
Ghosts have rounded heads and short vertical rounded bodies, with distinguishable red/cyan/pink/orange glow in normal play.
Frightened ghosts use a common pale-blue vulnerable appearance.
Returning ghosts use a visibly reduced pale form without the normal body.
Do not distinguish these states only by observer data or text.
State and identity are readable from moving silhouettes and color.
At fright expiry restore each ghost's own normal color; returning appearance takes precedence.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Active play.
Player moves around the maze.
Use a smoothly following, elevated perspective camera with visible top and side wall faces.
Keep the player within the central half of the view and enough surroundings to read upcoming intersections; at 720p show roughly 12 to 22 cell widths.
No fixed full-board orthographic map, first-person view, wall clipping, sustained occlusion or immediate snap at ordinary turns.
The maze slides naturally beneath a readable foreground character.
A wrap may reset the follow position promptly; no multi-second flight across the maze.
Menus/results may use a wider overview.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
An energizer, ghost capture, pineapple or life-loss event occurs.
Resolve the event.

Provide a short perceptible camera impulse and a distinct visual response: empowered-player change for energizer, returning-form change for ghost, pineapple overlay for fruit, and disappearance/death motion for life loss.
No missing feedback, permanent shaking, unreadable prolonged flash or camera displacement that prevents control.
A brief impulse settles within 0.5 seconds; the pineapple overlay clears within 1.5 seconds.
Repeated events remain bounded and Restart clears old effects.
Exact shake curves and shader implementations are free.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Any game menu or result is visible.
Read and use its controls.
Use a predominantly black background, large white heading and white/light-gray controls.
Keep title-menu choices left aligned
Options use labeled rows with left/right selectors and Back, Revert, Apply along the bottom.
Pause/result overlays preserve a dimmed or blurred world context.
No debug console as menu, clipped controls or style replaced by generic editor widgets.
The same visual language spans title, pause, options, win and loss.
Exact font family and pixel placement are free if visual hierarchy and required information remain clear.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A timed rule in this contract is active.
Observe its boundary or pause/resume.
Use active game time for movement, waves, frightened duration, release inactivity and fruit lifetime; the death interval is measured from lethal contact as defined in Section 6.4.
Timing acceptance tolerance is 0.15 seconds unless a rule specifies another tolerance.
No timer acceleration from render frame rate or elapsed paused time.
Paused world visuals stay still and resumed effects retain their remaining duration; menu feedback may animate.
Section 6.4 defines simultaneous-event priority, exact threshold boundaries and which clocks run in each phase.
The application is running.
Read the public observation output during normal play.
Expose truthful, current read-only observations of the visible phase, resources, actors, pickup presence, timers and usable menu targets described by the public observation contract.
No observation read may alter play, trigger a result, expose a cheat control or claim an outcome unsupported by the world.
Ordinary players use the normal game; all reported visible objects and controls match that view.
Missing gameplay remains explicitly unavailable in the untouched starter; alternative internal architectures are allowed.
The player is visible.
Move, turn and enter empowered play.
Use the supplied SM_Jaw mesh for the yellow upper/lower mouth, SM_Tooth for the pale teeth and SM_Eye for the dark eyes.
Use MI_Player, MI_Dot and MI_Eye for those respective surfaces, with M_Neon as their material base.
Keeping unused files in the project or substituting unrelated character art does not satisfy this requirement.
The supplied curved jaws, triangular teeth and spherical eyes form the visible animated player described by VISUAL-02.
Duplicate, transform, scale and animate the supplied parts; material parameter changes and derived instances are allowed if the specified colors and state feedback remain.
Retain the recognizable geometry.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
Ghosts are visible.
Observe normal, frightened and returning play.
Build the four normal ghost silhouettes from the supplied SM_GhostHead and SM_GhostBody.
Use MI_Red, MI_Cyan, MI_Pink and MI_Orange for their respective identities and MI_Frightened during vulnerability, retaining M_Neon as the base.
Unused resource references, generic replacement capsules or four identical normal colors do not satisfy the binding.
The supplied rounded heads and short bodies remain recognizable in normal/frightened play, with the distinctions required by VISUAL-03.
Scaling, animation and parameter changes are allowed.
The returning form may hide or reduce body parts to meet CAPTURE-02 and VISUAL-03.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
A pineapple is present.
Reach a fruit opportunity and collect it.
Use the supplied SM_FruitBody with MI_Fruit and SM_FruitCrown with MI_Crown as the visible maze pineapple, retaining M_Neon as their base.
A substitute primitive, unrelated model or decorative unused copy cannot replace the required fruit parts.
The faceted orange/gold fruit and green crown are visible during FRUIT-01.
Transforming, scaling, animating and tuning parameters is allowed while retaining the supplied silhouette.
The reward overlay and stage emblem may use a rendered image of these parts or separately authored artwork.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
The maze is visible.
Inspect active play.
Use M_Wall with its supplied T_WallEdge texture on the maze walls.
Use MI_Floor on the floor, MI_Gate on the home gate and MI_Dot on ordinary dots and energizers, retaining M_Neon as the base of these instances.
A resource present only in the Content Browser or an unrelated replacement material does not satisfy visible use.
The dark surfaces, blue wall edges, cyan gate and white pickups satisfy VISUAL-01.
Geometry, UV layout and collision are free.
Derived instances and shader/parameter adjustments are allowed while retaining the supplied material/texture contribution and the required colors, edge pattern and readability.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
The score/lives HUD is visible.
Start a run, lose a life or gain a life.
Use the supplied T_LifeIcon texture, or a raster/vector derived from the supplied life-icon SVG or PNG, for each life icon in HUD-01.
Either route fulfills the binding; using both is unnecessary.
Text-only lives, generic circles or unrelated icon art cannot replace the supplied shape; merely storing the icon is insufficient.
Yellow open-mouth icons remain recognizable and their count matches current lives.
Scale, space and animate icons to fit both required resolutions.
A derived raster or vector must retain the supplied shape and yellow color.
Reimporting raw files is not required.
The relevant Section 6.4 boundaries apply.
The project starts, runs, exits and starts again normally using the public instructions.
The main flow uses normal player input and does not rely on answer buttons, cheats or direct calls to gameplay outcomes.
Key entry points, text and controls are visible, discoverable, readable and operable.
Player actions have perceptible feedback that agrees with actual game state.
No severe error blocks the main flow.
Repeated runs from the same initial conditions are substantially stable.

qualification_test_scope: Distribution, evidence conversion and attribution invariants only; not gameplay semantic qualification.
